name: Philadelphia
summary: The birthplace of the nation — where independence was declared and signed — plus a great art museum and the country's best food market.

lodging.name: A hotel in Old City or Rittenhouse Square
lodging.blurb: Old City puts you steps from Independence Hall; Rittenhouse is the walkable dining hub.

foodMustTry.name: A cheesesteak
foodMustTry.blurb: Pat's and Geno's square off across one intersection; locals often send you to Dalessandro's instead.

foodMustTry.name: Reading Terminal Market
foodMustTry.blurb: A historic indoor market — roast pork sandwiches, Amish pretzels, and Bassetts ice cream.

days.label: Day 23 — Independence & the Rocky Steps
days.summary: The founding sites in the morning, art and a famous staircase after.

item.title: Independence Hall & the Liberty Bell
item.blurb: The room where the Declaration and Constitution were debated and signed, and the cracked bell across the street. Free timed tickets in peak season.

item.title: Lunch at Reading Terminal Market
item.blurb: Graze the stalls — roast pork with broccoli rabe is the local move.

item.title: Philadelphia Museum of Art & the Rocky Steps
item.blurb: Run the Rocky Steps, high-five the statue, then see a genuinely great collection inside.

days.label: Day 24 — Free Day
days.summary: Wander Old City and the Italian Market, or just rest before the capital.

freeMenu.title: Philadelphia's Magic Gardens
freeMenu.blurb: A whole block of mosaic folk art — gloriously weird.

freeMenu.title: South 9th Street Italian Market
freeMenu.blurb: The oldest continuously operating outdoor market in the country.

days.label: Day 25 — Drive to Washington, DC
days.summary: The final leg of the Northeast, into the capital.

commute.scenicNote: Optional history stop in Baltimore — Fort McHenry, where the national anthem was written.

stopsAlongWay.title: Fort McHenry, Baltimore
stopsAlongWay.blurb: The star fort whose defense inspired 'The Star-Spangled Banner.'
